newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Guyana could hold elections in October - officials.
newsitem.headline: Guyana could hold elections in October - officials.

text.p: Guyanese electoral officials said on Wednesday they were preparing for early parliamentary polls, probably in October this year.
Guyana's next national elections are not due until March next year but the sudden death of President Cheddi Jagan two months ago has hastened the electoral process, officials said.
Chief Election Officer Stanley Singh told Reuters plans for an election in early October were well advanced and that he would present interim President Samuel Hinds with a final report on Aug. 23.

Jagan's death at age 78 from heart disease swelled public support for his People's Progressive Party/Civic (PPP/Civic) alliance that won Guyana's first democratic elections for 28 years in October 1992.
Reflecting the wave of public sympathy following his death, Jagan's widow, Janet Jagan, was named prime minister and is widely tipped to lead the PPP/Civic alliance at the next elections.
Her opponent would most likely be the People's National Congress (PNC) party's Desmond Hoyte, who proceeded Jagan in the presidency.
